input.rationale: New sourced question from the configuration/eligibility axis, found while re-reading the conf-change paths. Propose-time validation decides leave-joint purely from len(Changes) == 0, while applyConfChange decides it from ConfChangeV2.LeaveJoint(), which for an empty change set is true only when the transition is Auto; an empty ChangeV2 with an explicit transition therefore passes validation while joint and is then treated as entering joint, which fails with the error config is already joint and panics. A focused probe against the real FSM confirmed the whole chain: entering a joint config with an explicit transition produced voters [1 2 3 4] against outgoing [1 2 3]; an empty JointExplicit ChangeV2 tested LeaveJoint false and EnterJoint ok true; stepping it as a MsgProp returned nil and appended EntryConfChangeV2 (the entry was not replaced by validation); and applying it panicked with config is already joint. I record this as a new investigation with a fixed experiment so the controller can produce the receipt, and I deliberately add no interpretation yet since the receipt does not exist.

investigations.question: Can an empty ConfChangeV2 whose Transition is explicit rather than auto pass the leader's propose-time configuration validation while the configuration is joint, and then panic the process when the application applies the committed entry? Propose-time validation tests len(Changes) == 0 for leave-joint, while applyConfChange tests ConfChangeV2.LeaveJoint(), which also requires the Auto transition.
investigations.hypothesis: The two leave-joint tests disagree for an empty change set with a non-Auto transition in a joint configuration: stepLeader treats it as a leave-joint request (wantsLeaveJoint true, alreadyJoint true, so no failed check and no entry replacement), but applyConfChange sees LeaveJoint false, takes the EnterJoint branch because EnterJoint reports ok for an explicit transition, calls Changer.EnterJoint on an already-joint tracker, receives the error and panics on the spot. The panic happens in the application's ApplyConfChange call for an entry the library accepted and committed.
investigations.discriminator: Confirm both halves separately: (a) the entry appended by the validated proposal still has type EntryConfChangeV2 rather than being replaced by EntryNormal, which shows validation accepted it; (b) applying that same ConfChangeV2 panics with config is already joint. If either half fails - for instance if some later guard replaces or drops the entry, or if EnterJoint returns ok false - the suspicion is refuted. Also check whether the Auto-transition empty change still leaves the joint config correctly, which would show the defect is specific to the explicit transition rather than to empty changes.

knowledge.statement: For an empty ConfChangeV2 with Transition = JointExplicit in a joint configuration: LeaveJoint() reports false and EnterJoint() reports ok true; stepLeader's propose-time validation computes wantsLeaveJoint from len(Changes) == 0 and, with alreadyJoint also true, produces no failed check, so the EntryConfChangeV2 is appended unchanged; applyConfChange then takes the EnterJoint branch and Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration, so applyConfChange panics with the error string config is already joint. Observed end to end on a real instance: after entering joint explicitly (voters [1 2 3 4] against outgoing [1 2 3]), the proposal step returned a nil error and left an EntryConfChangeV2 at the new last index, and applying it panicked with that exact string while the configuration was still joint.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is joint and the client supplies a ConfChangeV2 with an explicit (JointExplicit or JointImplicit) transition and no changes; propose-time validation is at its default (enabled), and the leader is a member so the proposal is not dropped for that reason. Validation only replaces the entry when it computes a failed check, which does not happen in this case because an empty change set is read as leave-joint regardless of transition. Distinct from the Auto-transition empty ChangeV2, which is the documented leave-joint idiom and takes the LeaveJoint path.

scope.description: Drive a real raft through entering a joint configuration and then through proposing and applying an empty ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition, recording whether propose-time validation keeps the entry and whether applying it panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and the library defaults; the joint configuration is entered by applying ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and a single add-node change, which is the normal EnterJoint path.

The malformed change is submitted through raft.Step as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 built by marshalling ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit}, which is exactly the input shape an application or client would produce.

ApplyConfChange is invoked directly on the same instance because the entry would not be committed on a quorum-less test instance; no production logic is modified and the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data.
excluded: Any claim about how a client library or etcd constructs its ConfChangeV2 messages; only the library's own acceptance and apply paths are measured.
The Auto-transition empty change, which is the supported leave-joint idiom and is not part of this comparison.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, applies ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]} and emits a setup event with the resulting voters, outgoing voters, the tested transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then marshals ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, and emits an event with the step error, how many entries were appended and the type of the last entry. Finally it calls applyConfChange on that same change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: Propose-time validation kept the entry as a configuration change rather than replacing it, so the library accepted the request.
Applying the accepted change panics because Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passes validation and panics on apply

investigations.question: In the ReadOnlySafe read-index flow, is a heartbeat response's Context validated against the outstanding read requests before it is used to confirm a read index, and what bounds the value used to slice unconfirmedReads?
investigations.hypothesis: Refined after resolving the gap: readOnly.recvAck does store a peer-supplied Context as a raw read-position ack with no check that the leader emitted it, and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the resulting quorum position without clamping. But every legal producer in this snapshot echoes a value the live leader's heartbeatCtx produced (handleHeartbeat is the sole writer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context), the readOnly instance is created only by raft.reset at a leadership transition, and the emitted position equals a message total that is non-decreasing, so the quorum position can never exceed confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in-model. The two consequences (slice-bounds panic; confirming a read no quorum observed) require a Context outside the set heartbeatCtx emitted, which no in-model producer supplies.
investigations.discriminator: Resolved: enumerate the sites that create the readOnly instance (only raft.reset, called from becomeFollower/becomeCandidate/becomeLeader) and the writers of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context (only handleHeartbeat, echoing m.Context). None can deliver a value the leader did not emit while its instance was live, because a readOnly instance is only live while its node is leader in a single term and cross-term responses are dropped before stepLeader. If a later source read showed any other readOnly reassignment or Context producer (e.g. an application-visible heartbeat context), the in-model claim would revive.

gaps.question: Is there any legal producer in this snapshot (or a mixed-version cluster running the v3.6.0 node) that delivers MsgHeartbeatResp.Context values the current leader's heartbeatCtx never emitted for its live readOnly instance - for example an in-flight heartbeat response that survives a same-term readOnly recreation, or a peer that echoes a context from a different node/term?

history.question: In the ReadOnlySafe read-index flow, is a heartbeat response's Context validated against the outstanding read requests before it is used to confirm a read index, and what bounds the value used to slice unconfirmedReads?
history.hypothesis: readOnly.recvAck decodes the peer-supplied Context as a raw uint64 read position with no check that it was produced by heartbeatCtx for an outstanding request, and readOnly.maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the quorum position without clamping. A Context larger than the number of outstanding reads would then confirm reads no quorum actually acknowledged, or panic with a slice-bounds error.
history.discriminator: Identify any legal (non-Byzantine) producer of MsgHeartbeatResp whose Context is not a value the leader's own heartbeatCtx emitted for the current readOnly lifetime. If none exists, the premise fails and the behavior is unreachable in the crash-fault model; if one exists (or if the leader itself can supply a stale/oversized value), the safety and liveness consequences apply in-model.

investigations.question: When a MsgReadIndex is postponed because the leader has not committed an entry in its term, is that queued duty eventually completed with a read index at least as large as the one the same request would have received at admission, including when the queue survives loss and later reacquisition of leadership (and when the node is deposed, removed, or restarted in between)?
investigations.hypothesis: The queue is not cleared by raft.reset (term or state change), so a request admitted at term T is released later, while the node is leader again at term T' > T. Release recomputes the index from the live r.raftLog.committed, and every write to raftLog.committed is non-decreasing (commitTo refuses to lower it; loadState and log restore are guarded to only raise it above the current value). The completed read index is therefore >= the committed index at admission, so the surviving duty cannot produce a stale read index.
investigations.discriminator: Look for any site that lowers raftLog.committed after a request is queued, or any release path that reuses an index captured before admission instead of reading the live commit index. None would mean the stale-index suspicion is defeated; a lowering site or a cached-index release would revive it. Secondary: whether the queue can be released while the node is not the current leader (releasePendingReadIndexMessages is only called from the leader's MsgAppResp path and re-checks committedEntryInCurrentTerm).

investigations.question: Once a leader puts a follower's Progress into StateSnapshot, which actors can restore replication to that follower, and is there an enabled repair when the follower applied the snapshot but the corresponding MsgAppResp is lost?
investigations.hypothesis: The state pauses appends (IsPaused is unconditionally true in StateSnapshot), so the only exits are: the leader's MsgAppResp handler advancing pr.Match and hitting the StateSnapshot recovery arm, or an application ReportSnapshot call arriving as MsgSnapStatus. Both require an external event, so a follower that applied the snapshot whose MsgAppResp was lost, with no ReportSnapshot from the application, would remain paused.
investigations.discriminator: Check whether the library reaches StateSnapshot without a matching application report obligation, and whether any timer or heartbeat path can exit StateSnapshot on its own. The README/Ready contract and the ReportSnapshot doc place that obligation on the application; a self-repair path that does not exist in the leader code would mean the duty is only repairable externally.

investigations.question: Can a caller that follows the documented ReadIndex retry contract grow the leader's per-request read state without bound? Specifically: does each retried MsgReadIndex (same RequestCtx) add one unconfirmedReads entry and one heartbeat broadcast that are never collapsed, and is there any in-model state (leader isolated from a quorum, checkQuorum disabled or not yet fired) under which the entries are never confirmed and never dropped?
investigations.hypothesis: readOnly.addRequest appends unconditionally, without the context-keyed deduplication the v3.6.0 implementation performed, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse calls bcastHeartbeat for every admitted request. Entries leave unconfirmedReads only when a quorum acks the recorded position (readOnly.maybeAdvance), so a leader that cannot obtain quorum acks retains every retried request and rebroadcasts for each, which grows memory and generated traffic with the number of caller retries rather than with the number of distinct reads.
investigations.discriminator: Establish whether the retry contract permits an unbounded number of retries with an identical RequestCtx while the leader stays in StateLeader without quorum confirmation (checkQuorum disabled, or the retry rate exceeding the election timeout). If that state is reachable under permitted use, the growth is an in-model bounded-resource concern; if the caller is required to bound retries or the leader always confirms or steps down first, the behavior is benign and the suspicion is refuted.

investigations.question: Can a node that the configuration no longer contains have its proposals accepted and committed after it learns of a new leader? node.run() blocks the proposal channel only until the next observed leader change, and describes that behaviour as unsound; do the raft handlers then accept a proposal whose sender is not a member, and is sender eligibility a library duty or a caller duty?
investigations.hypothesis: The Node facade re-enables the proposal channel whenever lead != r.lead and the new lead is not None, regardless of the node's own membership, so a removed node's client can keep proposing after any leadership change; the proposal is then forwarded by stepFollower to the current leader, and stepLeader's MsgProp handler writes it without consulting Progress[m.From], so the entry is appended and can be committed even though the sender is not in the configuration.
investigations.discriminator: Decide who owns sender eligibility: if the library's documented contract places authorization on the caller (the application), then accepting a proposal from a non-member is out of scope and the suspicion is refuted; if node.go's own stated intent to block proposals from a removed node is the contract, then re-enabling the channel on a leader change is a defect. Concretely: check whether any handler or contract rejects MsgProp from an id absent from the configuration, and whether the application can observe that its request came from a removed member.

gaps.question: Does any part of the library contract, node documentation or Ready/Propose API make sender eligibility the caller's responsibility (so that a leader accepting a non-member's proposal is intended), or is node.go's 'block incoming proposals' the intended guarantee, which the leader-change path then breaks?

knowledge.statement: For ReadOnlySafe, the leader confirms reads as follows: sendMsgReadIndexResponse calls readOnly.addRequest(committed, m), self-acks by recvAck(r.id, heartbeatCtx()) and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in 8 little-endian bytes; on each MsgHeartbeatResp with non-empty Context the leader calls readOnly.recvAck(m.From, m.Context), which stores max(existing, binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(Context)) in acks[m.From]; maybeAdvance computes newConfirmedReads = quorum.JointConfig.CommittedIndex(ro) over acks (unacked voters count as 0), and if newConfirmedReads > confirmedReads it returns unconfirmedReads[:newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads] and advances confirmedReads. No comparison is made between the received Context and any value the leader emitted.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; the ack map and unconfirmedReads are per readOnly instance, recreated by raft.reset on each state/term change. Values in acks are positions (counts of admitted read requests), not log indexes.

knowledge.statement: Under the framework's own producers, every value written into readOnly.acks equals a value heartbeatCtx produced for this readOnly lifetime, and heartbeatCtx values are non-decreasing and at most the number of admitted read requests. Therefore for a faithful cluster the quorum position newConfirmedReads never exceeds confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads); the slicing in maybeAdvance is in range and each confirmed read corresponds to a heartbeat sent after that read was admitted.
knowledge.conditions: All peers echo MsgHeartbeatResp.Context exactly as produced by the leader's heartbeatCtx (the only context the checked-in follower path writes, via handleHeartbeat), and the leader's readOnly is not recreated between request admission and response handling except across state/term changes, after which lower-term responses are ignored by raft.Step.

knowledge.statement: In this snapshot the ReadOnlySafe ack bookkeeping is in-model consistent: (1) r.readOnly is reassigned only in raft.reset (:809) and reset is called only by becomeFollower (:893), becomeCandidate (:908, term+1) and becomeLeader (:939, the candidate's term), so a readOnly instance is live only while its node is leader at one term; (2) raft.Step drops a lower-term MsgHeartbeatResp before dispatch (:1158-1175); (3) the only producer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context is handleHeartbeat (:1837), echoing the leader's heartbeat Context, and vote contexts are sent on MsgVote (:1071); (4) heartbeatCtx emits exactly confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads), which addRequest only grows and maybeAdvance preserves. Therefore every value in readOnly.acks is at most the current message total, newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads can never exceed len(unconfirmedReads), and each returned read corresponds to a heartbeat emitted after that request was admitted and acknowledged by a quorum. The slice-bounds panic and premature confirmation observed when a probe supplied an out-of-contract Context are not reachable through the library's own producers.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; leadership terms strictly increase (becomeCandidate panics from StateLeader and increments the term); cluster members run this library's follower path (including a v3.6.0 node, which also echoes m.Context); no two leaders exist in the same term. Excludes a peer or intermediary that fabricates or corrupts MsgHeartbeatResp.Context, which is outside the crash-fault model.

knowledge.statement: pendingReadIndexMessages lifecycle for MsgReadIndex on a leader: in stepLeader (:1355-1372) a request is answered immediately when the cluster is a singleton or when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, and is otherwise appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages without a term stamp; raft.reset (:781-812) does not clear the slice, so it survives step-downs, re-elections and being removed from the config; releasePendingReadIndexMessages (:2127-2144) is invoked only from the leader's MsgAppResp fast path after maybeCommit() returns true (:1546-1556), returns early with an error log if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() no longer holds, and otherwise swaps the slice out and passes each stored message to sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which captures the index as r.raftLog.committed at that moment (ReadOnlySafe also re-enters the addRequest/heartbeat confirmation flow for it).
knowledge.conditions: Node acts as leader; r.raftLog.committed is the only source of the read index. Commit index monotonicity holds because commitTo (:322-330) assigns only when l.committed < tocommit, log restore is reached only when the snapshot index exceeds the current committed (log.go :463-470 guard), and loadState (:2037-2047) rejects any state.commit below the current committed.

knowledge.statement: Leader-side StateSnapshot handling: maybeSendSnapshot (:666-694) refuses to send while pr.RecentActive is false, and otherwise calls pr.BecomeSnapshot(snapshotIndex) which sets State=StateSnapshot, PendingSnapshot=Next-1 and pauses the follower. While in that state Progress.IsPaused() returns true unconditionally (tracker/progress.go :262-282), so maybeSendAppend returns immediately, bcastAppend is a no-op for that peer, and the MsgHeartbeatResp branch's sendAppend (:1588-1596) also sends nothing. Exactly two producers can leave the state: (1) stepLeader's MsgAppResp handler (:1518-1546) when pr.MaybeUpdate(m.GetIndex()) is true (m.Index strictly greater than pr.Match) and then pr.Match+1 >= raftLog.firstIndex(), which runs BecomeProbe followed by BecomeReplicate; and (2) stepLeader's MsgSnapStatus handler (:1612-1634) from the application's ReportSnapshot, which returns early unless pr.State == StateSnapshot, then clears PendingSnapshot when the snapshot failed and calls BecomeProbe either way.
knowledge.conditions: Node is leader; the peer is a tracked follower or learner. The follower emits the MsgAppResp either by applying the snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its last index) or by ignoring an obsolete snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its committed index). ReportSnapshot reaches the leader as MsgSnapStatus only when the application calls it.

knowledge.statement: When readOnly.recvAck is given an 8-byte Context value larger than the number of outstanding read requests, the ReadOnlySafe confirmation path behaves as follows in this snapshot. With a quorum of such values (leader self-ack position 1 plus two peers at position 2^40, voters {1,2,3}), readOnly.maybeAdvance panics inside its slice expression: 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'. With a single such value (two admitted reads, leader self-ack position 2, an honest peer at position 1, one peer at position 2 that received no heartbeat carrying position 2), maybeAdvance does not panic and instead returns both admitted reads (advanced=2, confirmed_reads=2), i.e. it confirms a read index that the forged voter never observed. Both outcomes were observed with the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads driven directly; no raft instance, network or storage was involved.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; ack values are injected directly into the unexported readOnly via recvAck instead of being produced by the library's follower path (handleHeartbeat), which is the out-of-contract premise. Quorum position is the median of stored acks because CommittedIndex is evaluated over quorum.JointConfig{1,2,3},nil. Does not apply to ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which does not use the ack map.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe admission and growth, in this snapshot: every MsgReadIndex that reaches a leader is admitted individually - if the cluster is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds one entry to readOnly.unconfirmedReads via readOnly.addRequest (which appends without any lookup of an existing request with the same context) and then broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() does not hold, the raw message is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and released (one response per queued message) only later, each release again going through addRequest plus a heartbeat broadcast. Entries are removed from unconfirmedReads only by readOnly.maybeAdvance, which requires the quorum ack position to exceed confirmedReads. Nothing in the admission path inspects the RequestCtx, so N retries with an identical context produce N unconfirmedReads entries and N heartbeat broadcasts.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe, leader in StateLeader. The behavior is a property of admission, independent of whether the reads are eventually confirmed; under a healthy quorum each retry is confirmed quickly, so the queue stays short. The node-level contract that makes retries the caller's duty is stated at node.go:222-223 ('request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries').

knowledge.statement: For a real raft leader of a three-voter configuration that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, repeated local MsgReadIndex submissions with an identical RequestCtx accumulate without bound in pendingReadIndexMessages and are not reclaimed by an authority transition. Measured: with the node at term 1, committed 0, lastIndex 1, CheckQuorum false and the default ReadOnlySafe option, 64 retries produced pendingReadIndexMessages length 64 (one entry per retry, no collapsing) and readOnly.unconfirmedReads length 0 while the node was still StateLeader; after a higher-term MsgHeartbeat deposed it to StateFollower the queue was still length 64 and unconfirmedReads still 0. The growth count equals the retry count, so neither the library nor raft.reset (which recreates readOnly but leaves the queue) bounds or clears it.
knowledge.conditions: Library defaults as built by newTestRaft without CheckQuorum (false) and with ReadOnlySafe; the environment delivers no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp, modelling a leader partitioned from its quorum. Callers retry with the same RequestCtx, which node.go:218-224 tells them to do and does not bound. Scope: the queued path (leader has not committed in its term); the admitted path is subject to the same per-request, context-blind admission and additionally broadcasts a heartbeat per request.

knowledge.statement: When a two-voter leader that has accumulated 64 queued read requests (pendingReadIndexMessages length 64, committed 0, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() false, unconfirmedReads 0) finally commits in its term through the normal MsgAppResp fast path, that single step empties the queue and re-admits everything: pendingReadIndexMessages becomes 0, readOnly.unconfirmedReads becomes 64 and 64 MsgHeartbeat messages are produced in the same step, with committed 1 and in_term true afterwards. So the retained queue is not merely passive memory: on release it becomes one read request plus one outbound heartbeat per queued entry, all at once.
knowledge.conditions: Library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the commit is produced by stepping the leader's own MsgAppResp and then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages - the harness never calls the release function directly. No heartbeat response is delivered afterwards, so the re-admitted requests stay unconfirmed.

knowledge.statement: CheckQuorum bounds the growth window of accumulated read requests but does not reclaim them. With CheckQuorum enabled on a three-voter leader at election timeout 3 and no peer messages, 24 same-context retries submitted over three ticks ended with the node already StateFollower (the quorum view was lost and it stepped down within the election timeout), and eight further read requests submitted after the step-down left pendingReadIndexMessages at exactly its prior length of 24 with readOnly.unconfirmedReads 0, because a leaderless follower drops ReadIndex messages instead of queueing them. So under CheckQuorum the accumulation stops when the leader steps down, whereas with CheckQuorum disabled (the library default) nothing stops it; in both configurations the state already accumulated is retained.
knowledge.conditions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum true, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe, no peer messages delivered. Retries use an identical RequestCtx (the documented retry pattern). The control says nothing about a network partition or about ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which requires CheckQuorum.

knowledge.statement: The read state a quorum-less leader retains is caller-controlled in size. With CheckQuorum false over voters {1,2,3}, 64 ReadIndex requests each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx were all retained in pendingReadIndexMessages: pending 64, summed retained Data length 262144 bytes, and 64 distinct backing buffers, so the total is genuine per-request retention rather than one shared slice counted 64 times. The retained payload per leader therefore equals the number of accepted requests times the caller-chosen context size, with no library-side limit on either factor.
knowledge.conditions: No MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every request takes the queued path; each request carries a distinct buffer, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit). The count covers only the entry Data payloads held in pendingReadIndexMessages, not message structs, slice headers or allocator overhead, and no deployment memory limit is claimed.

knowledge.statement: Proposal eligibility handling in this snapshot. In node.run, the proposal send channel is set to nil when the node learns that it was removed from the configuration by a config change it applied (only when it was in the config before), which blocks incoming proposals, but it is re-assigned to the real channel whenever the observed leader changes to a non-None value, independently of the node's membership; the accompanying in-tree comment states that this is not sound and likely has bugs. On the raft side, stepFollower's MsgProp case forwards the message to r.lead without any membership test, and stepLeader's MsgProp case only checks whether the leader itself is still a member (Progress[r.id] == nil) before appending, so a proposal whose From is not in the configuration is written to the log if it reaches the leader.

knowledge.statement: The read state that a leader accumulates is volatile and cannot outlive the process. newRaft builds it fresh (readOnly via newReadOnly at raft.go:462; pendingReadIndexMessages is a slice field of the raft struct, raft.go:430-435, left nil), the only writers are the stepLeader MsgReadIndex append and the release path that swaps the slice out, and the Storage interface exposes only InitialState, Entries, Term, FirstIndex, LastIndex and Snapshot (storage.go:48-95) with no read-state member; there is no ReadState or readStates reference in storage.go or raftpb. investigations.question: In the ReadOnlySafe read-index flow, is a heartbeat response's Context validated against the outstanding read requests before it is used to confirm a read index, and what bounds the value used to slice unconfirmedReads?
investigations.hypothesis: Refined after resolving the gap: readOnly.recvAck does store a peer-supplied Context as a raw read-position ack with no check that the leader emitted it, and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the resulting quorum position without clamping. But every legal producer in this snapshot echoes a value the live leader's heartbeatCtx produced (handleHeartbeat is the sole writer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context), the readOnly instance is created only by raft.reset at a leadership transition, and the emitted position equals a message total that is non-decreasing, so the quorum position can never exceed confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in-model. The two consequences (slice-bounds panic; confirming a read no quorum observed) require a Context outside the set heartbeatCtx emitted, which no in-model producer supplies.

None can deliver a value the leader did not emit while its instance was live, because a readOnly instance is only live while its node is leader in a single term and cross-term responses are dropped before stepLeader. knowledge.statement: For ReadOnlySafe, the leader confirms reads as follows: sendMsgReadIndexResponse calls readOnly.addRequest(committed, m), self-acks by recvAck(r.id, heartbeatCtx()) and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in 8 little-endian bytes; on each MsgHeartbeatResp with non-empty Context the leader calls readOnly.recvAck(m.From, m.Context), which stores max(existing, binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(Context)) in acks[m.From]; maybeAdvance computes newConfirmedReads = quorum.JointConfig.CommittedIndex(ro) over acks (unacked voters count as 0), and if newConfirmedReads > confirmedReads it returns unconfirmedReads[:newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads] and advances confirmedReads. No comparison is made between the received Context and any value the leader emitted.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; the ack map and unconfirmedReads are per readOnly instance, recreated by raft.reset on each state/term change. Values in acks are positions (counts of admitted read requests), not log indexes.

knowledge.statement: Under the framework's own producers, every value written into readOnly.acks equals a value heartbeatCtx produced for this readOnly lifetime, and heartbeatCtx values are non-decreasing and at most the number of admitted read requests. Therefore for a faithful cluster the quorum position newConfirmedReads never exceeds confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads); the slicing in maybeAdvance is in range and each confirmed read corresponds to a heartbeat sent after that read was admitted.
knowledge.conditions: All peers echo MsgHeartbeatResp.Context exactly as produced by the leader's heartbeatCtx (the only context the checked-in follower path writes, via handleHeartbeat), and the leader's readOnly is not recreated between request admission and response handling except across state/term changes, after which lower-term responses are ignored by raft.Step.

knowledge.statement: In this snapshot the ReadOnlySafe ack bookkeeping is in-model consistent: (1) r.readOnly is reassigned only in raft.reset (:809) and reset is called only by becomeFollower (:893), becomeCandidate (:908, term+1) and becomeLeader (:939, the candidate's term), so a readOnly instance is live only while its node is leader at one term; (2) raft.Step drops a lower-term MsgHeartbeatResp before dispatch (:1158-1175); (3) the only producer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context is handleHeartbeat (:1837), echoing the leader's heartbeat Context, and vote contexts are sent on MsgVote (:1071); (4) heartbeatCtx emits exactly confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads), which addRequest only grows and maybeAdvance preserves. Therefore every value in readOnly.acks is at most the current message total, newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads can never exceed len(unconfirmedReads), and each returned read corresponds to a heartbeat emitted after that request was admitted and acknowledged by a quorum. The slice-bounds panic and premature confirmation observed when a probe supplied an out-of-contract Context are not reachable through the library's own producers.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; leadership terms strictly increase (becomeCandidate panics from StateLeader and increments the term); cluster members run this library's follower path (including a v3.6.0 node, which also echoes m.Context); no two leaders exist in the same term. Excludes a peer or intermediary that fabricates or corrupts MsgHeartbeatResp.Context, which is outside the crash-fault model.

knowledge.statement: pendingReadIndexMessages lifecycle for MsgReadIndex on a leader: in stepLeader (:1355-1372) a request is answered immediately when the cluster is a singleton or when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, and is otherwise appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages without a term stamp; raft.reset (:781-812) does not clear the slice, so it survives step-downs, re-elections and being removed from the config; releasePendingReadIndexMessages (:2127-2144) is invoked only from the leader's MsgAppResp fast path after maybeCommit() returns true (:1546-1556), returns early with an error log if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() no longer holds, and otherwise swaps the slice out and passes each stored message to sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which captures the index as r.raftLog.committed at that moment (ReadOnlySafe also re-enters the addRequest/heartbeat confirmation flow for it).
knowledge.conditions: Node acts as leader; r.raftLog.committed is the only source of the read index. Commit index monotonicity holds because commitTo (:322-330) assigns only when l.committed < tocommit, log restore is reached only when the snapshot index exceeds the current committed (log.go :463-470 guard), and loadState (:2037-2047) rejects any state.commit below the current committed.

knowledge.statement: Leader-side StateSnapshot handling: maybeSendSnapshot (:666-694) refuses to send while pr.RecentActive is false, and otherwise calls pr.BecomeSnapshot(snapshotIndex) which sets State=StateSnapshot, PendingSnapshot=Next-1 and pauses the follower. While in that state Progress.IsPaused() returns true unconditionally (tracker/progress.go :262-282), so maybeSendAppend returns immediately, bcastAppend is a no-op for that peer, and the MsgHeartbeatResp branch's sendAppend (:1588-1596) also sends nothing. Exactly two producers can leave the state: (1) stepLeader's MsgAppResp handler (:1518-1546) when pr.MaybeUpdate(m.GetIndex()) is true (m.Index strictly greater than pr.Match) and then pr.Match+1 >= raftLog.firstIndex(), which runs BecomeProbe followed by BecomeReplicate; and (2) stepLeader's MsgSnapStatus handler (:1612-1634) from the application's ReportSnapshot, which returns early unless pr.State == StateSnapshot, then clears PendingSnapshot when the snapshot failed and calls BecomeProbe either way.
knowledge.conditions: Node is leader; the peer is a tracked follower or learner. The follower emits the MsgAppResp either by applying the snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its last index) or by ignoring an obsolete snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its committed index). ReportSnapshot reaches the leader as MsgSnapStatus only when the application calls it.

knowledge.statement: When readOnly.recvAck is given an 8-byte Context value larger than the number of outstanding read requests, the ReadOnlySafe confirmation path behaves as follows in this snapshot. With a quorum of such values (leader self-ack position 1 plus two peers at position 2^40, voters {1,2,3}), readOnly.maybeAdvance panics inside its slice expression: 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'. With a single such value (two admitted reads, leader self-ack position 2, an honest peer at position 1, one peer at position 2 that received no heartbeat carrying position 2), maybeAdvance does not panic and instead returns both admitted reads (advanced=2, confirmed_reads=2), i.e. it confirms a read index that the forged voter never observed. Both outcomes were observed with the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads driven directly; no raft instance, network or storage was involved.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; ack values are injected directly into the unexported readOnly via recvAck instead of being produced by the library's follower path (handleHeartbeat), which is the out-of-contract premise. Quorum position is the median of stored acks because CommittedIndex is evaluated over quorum.JointConfig{1,2,3},nil. Does not apply to ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which does not use the ack map.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe admission and growth, in this snapshot: every MsgReadIndex that reaches a leader is admitted individually - if the cluster is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds one entry to readOnly.unconfirmedReads via readOnly.addRequest (which appends without any lookup of an existing request with the same context) and then broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() does not hold, the raw message is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and released (one response per queued message) only later, each release again going through addRequest plus a heartbeat broadcast. Entries are removed from unconfirmedReads only by readOnly.maybeAdvance, which requires the quorum ack position to exceed confirmedReads. Nothing in the admission path inspects the RequestCtx, so N retries with an identical context produce N unconfirmedReads entries and N heartbeat broadcasts.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe, leader in StateLeader. The behavior is a property of admission, independent of whether the reads are eventually confirmed; under a healthy quorum each retry is confirmed quickly, so the queue stays short. The node-level contract that makes retries the caller's duty is stated at node.go:222-223 ('request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries').

knowledge.statement: For a real raft leader of a three-voter configuration that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, repeated local MsgReadIndex submissions with an identical RequestCtx accumulate without bound in pendingReadIndexMessages and are not reclaimed by an authority transition. Measured: with the node at term 1, committed 0, lastIndex 1, CheckQuorum false and the default ReadOnlySafe option, 64 retries produced pendingReadIndexMessages length 64 (one entry per retry, no collapsing) and readOnly.unconfirmedReads length 0 while the node was still StateLeader; after a higher-term MsgHeartbeat deposed it to StateFollower the queue was still length 64 and unconfirmedReads still 0. The growth count equals the retry count, so neither the library nor raft.reset (which recreates readOnly but leaves the queue) bounds or clears it.
knowledge.conditions: Library defaults as built by newTestRaft without CheckQuorum (false) and with ReadOnlySafe; the environment delivers no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp, modelling a leader partitioned from its quorum. Callers retry with the same RequestCtx, which node.go:218-224 tells them to do and does not bound. Scope: the queued path (leader has not committed in its term); the admitted path is subject to the same per-request, context-blind admission and additionally broadcasts a heartbeat per request.

knowledge.statement: When a two-voter leader that has accumulated 64 queued read requests (pendingReadIndexMessages length 64, committed 0, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() false, unconfirmedReads 0) finally commits in its term through the normal MsgAppResp fast path, that single step empties the queue and re-admits everything: pendingReadIndexMessages becomes 0, readOnly.unconfirmedReads becomes 64 and 64 MsgHeartbeat messages are produced in the same step, with committed 1 and in_term true afterwards. So the retained queue is not merely passive memory: on release it becomes one read request plus one outbound heartbeat per queued entry, all at once.
knowledge.conditions: Library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the commit is produced by stepping the leader's own MsgAppResp and then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages - the harness never calls the release function directly. No heartbeat response is delivered afterwards, so the re-admitted requests stay unconfirmed.

knowledge.statement: CheckQuorum bounds the growth window of accumulated read requests but does not reclaim them. With CheckQuorum enabled on a three-voter leader at election timeout 3 and no peer messages, 24 same-context retries submitted over three ticks ended with the node already StateFollower (the quorum view was lost and it stepped down within the election timeout), and eight further read requests submitted after the step-down left pendingReadIndexMessages at exactly its prior length of 24 with readOnly.unconfirmedReads 0, because a leaderless follower drops ReadIndex messages instead of queueing them. So under CheckQuorum the accumulation stops when the leader steps down, whereas with CheckQuorum disabled (the library default) nothing stops it; in both configurations the state already accumulated is retained.
knowledge.conditions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum true, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe, no peer messages delivered. Retries use an identical RequestCtx (the documented retry pattern). The control says nothing about a network partition or about ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which requires CheckQuorum.

knowledge.statement: The read state a quorum-less leader retains is caller-controlled in size. With CheckQuorum false over voters {1,2,3}, 64 ReadIndex requests each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx were all retained in pendingReadIndexMessages: pending 64, summed retained Data length 262144 bytes, and 64 distinct backing buffers, so the total is genuine per-request retention rather than one shared slice counted 64 times. The retained payload per leader therefore equals the number of accepted requests times the caller-chosen context size, with no library-side limit on either factor.
knowledge.conditions: No MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every request takes the queued path; each request carries a distinct buffer, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit). The count covers only the entry Data payloads held in pendingReadIndexMessages, not message structs, slice headers or allocator overhead, and no deployment memory limit is claimed.

knowledge.statement: Proposal eligibility handling in this snapshot. In node.run, the proposal send channel is set to nil when the node learns that it was removed from the configuration by a config change it applied (only when it was in the config before), which blocks incoming proposals, but it is re-assigned to the real channel whenever the observed leader changes to a non-None value, independently of the node's membership; the accompanying in-tree comment states that this is not sound and likely has bugs. On the raft side, stepFollower's MsgProp case forwards the message to r.lead without any membership test, and stepLeader's MsgProp case only checks whether the leader itself is still a member (Progress[r.id] == nil) before appending, so a proposal whose From is not in the configuration is written to the log if it reaches the leader.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the Node facade (the goroutine-driven run loop) plus the raft handlers; RawNode users bypass the facade and step messages directly, and DisableProposalForwarding only affects followers that are members. The behaviour concerns eligibility of the proposer, not voting or commit quorums, which continue to use the configuration.

knowledge.statement: The documented MsgProp contract assigns no proposer-eligibility check to the library. doc.go states that when MsgProp is passed to the leader's Step method the leader first calls appendEntry to append entries to its log and then broadcasts them, that MsgProp is dropped by a candidate, and that on a follower it is stored with the sender's ID and later forwarded to the leader; the contract is about redirection of proposals, not about authorizing the proposer. Consistently, the checked-in handlers do not consult membership for proposals: stepFollower forwards MsgProp to r.lead, and stepLeader's MsgProp case checks only whether the leader itself is still a member. The Node facade does block its own proposal channel when it applies a config change that removes it, but that is a local best-effort whose accompanying comment calls it unsound and notes that the channel is reset on a leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the Node and RawNode APIs in this snapshot, including a mixed cluster: the leader cannot in general verify the sender's identity beyond the self-declared From field, and the documented contract does not ask it to. Eligibility of voters and commit quorums still use the configuration; only proposer eligibility is unguarded.

knowledge.statement: The read state that a leader accumulates is volatile and cannot outlive the process. newRaft builds it fresh (readOnly via newReadOnly at raft.go:462; pendingReadIndexMessages is a slice field of the raft struct, raft.go:430-435, left nil), the only writers are the stepLeader MsgReadIndex append and the release path that swaps the slice out, and the Storage interface exposes only InitialState, Entries, Term, FirstIndex, LastIndex and Snapshot (storage.go:48-95) with no read-state member; there is no ReadState or readStates reference in storage.go or raftpb. A restarted node therefore begins with an empty pending queue and an empty ack map, so any accumulation is bounded by the process lifetime and cleared incidentally by a restart, even though the library never clears it while running.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to both StartNode and RestartNode paths, since both build the raft through newRaft; the statement is about library-side state only and says nothing about how a restart interacts with the caller's retries. It bounds the retry-growth finding rather than contradicting it: within one process lifetime there is still no bound and no reclamation.

knowledge.statement: For an empty ConfChangeV2 with Transition = JointExplicit in a joint configuration: LeaveJoint() reports false and EnterJoint() reports ok true; stepLeader's propose-time validation computes wantsLeaveJoint from len(Changes) == 0 and, with alreadyJoint also true, produces no failed check, so the EntryConfChangeV2 is appended unchanged; applyConfChange then takes the EnterJoint branch and Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration, so applyConfChange panics with the error string config is already joint. Observed end to end on a real instance: after entering joint explicitly (voters [1 2 3 4] against outgoing [1 2 3]), the proposal step returned a nil error and left an EntryConfChangeV2 at the new last index, and applying it panicked with that exact string while the configuration was still joint.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is joint and the client supplies a ConfChangeV2 with an explicit (JointExplicit or JointImplicit) transition and no changes; propose-time validation is at its default (enabled), and the leader is a member so the proposal is not dropped for that reason. Validation only replaces the entry when it computes a failed check, which does not happen in this case because an empty change set is read as leave-joint regardless of transition. Distinct from the Auto-transition empty ChangeV2, which is the documented leave-joint idiom and takes the LeaveJoint path.

scope.description: Drive a real raft leader that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements and repeatedly submit ReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, measuring the queued read state and whether it survives being deposed.

Lease-based reads, which never enter the pending queue or ack structures.

basis.prefix: The test builds a real raft via newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate() then becomeLeader(), and emits a setup event recording state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, the read-only option and voter count. It then calls raft.Step 64 times with a local MsgReadIndex carrying the same RequestCtx, clearing r.msgs and r.msgsAfterAppend after each step, and emits the queue lengths. Finally it steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 to depose the leader and emits the queue lengths again to show whether the queued duty survives the authority transition.

comparisons.description: 64 same-context retries are all queued as separate pending read requests, matching the round count and showing no collapsing or bound.
After being deposed by a higher term, the node is a follower but the queued read requests are still retained, so the accumulation is not cancelled by the authority transition.

scope.description: Measure both admission outcomes of the ReadOnlySafe read path for a caller retrying ReadIndex with an identical RequestCtx: the queued path of a leader that has not committed in its term, and the admitted path of a leader that has committed in its term but whose follower stops acknowledging heartbeats.
assumptions: Both nodes are real raft instances built with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the queued case uses voters {1,2,3} and the admitted case {1,2}.

For the admitted case the leader's commit is produced the normal way - the leader's own MsgAppResp is stepped from msgsAfterAppend and then node 2 acknowledges the empty entry - so committedEntryInCurrentTerm() becomes true without any artificial state.

After that point no MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'followers stop acknowledging'; outbound messages are counted and then cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state and broadcasts are counted explicitly.
excluded: Any claim about a particular caller's retry timer, and any claim about lease-based reads.
Reads that are eventually confirmed: the point is what the leader accumulates while they are not.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexPendingGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, emits a setup event (state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, read-only option, voter count), steps 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic, emits the queue lengths, then steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 and emits the queue lengths again. TestAssuranceReadIndexAdmittedGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it, steps the self-ack messages out of msgsAfterAppend and then node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry so the leader commits in its term, emits a setup event including committedEntryInCurrentTerm(), then steps the same 64 same-context MsgReadIndex messages while counting MsgHeartbeat messages per round, and emits unconfirmedReads, broadcast count, pending length, confirmedReads and state.

comparisons.description: Queued path: 64 same-context retries are all retained as separate pending read requests.
Queued path: the accumulated requests survive deposition to StateFollower unchanged.
Admitted path: with the leader committed in its term but no heartbeat acknowledgements, 64 retries add 64 unconfirmed read requests.
Admitted path: each of the 64 retries also broadcasts one heartbeat, so retries cost outbound messages in addition to retained state.

knowledge.assertion: admission is per request and context-blind, and each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by deposition

scope.description: Measure the drain burst: accumulate queued read requests on a leader that has not committed in its term, then let it commit in its term and record what the release path does with the whole queue in that one step.
assumptions: Real raft instance built with library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe) over voters {1,2}, so the leader becomes committed in its term once its own ack and node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry are delivered.
64 ReadIndex retries with an identical RequestCtx are submitted before any acknowledgement is delivered, so all of them take the queued path.

The commit is produced through the normal leadership path (self MsgAppResp stepped with From=1, then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex), which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages; the harness does not call the release function directly.
excluded: Any claim about a network schedule or about a caller's retry timer; only the step-local effect is measured.
Whether the released reads are then confirmed: no heartbeat response is delivered, so the re-admitted entries stay unconfirmed.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, submits 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic each round, and emits a setup event with the queue length, committed index, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and unconfirmed length. It then steps a MsgAppResp with From=1 at lastIndex and node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the leader fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages, and emits the post-commit event with committed, in_term, queue length, unconfirmed length, the number of MsgHeartbeat messages produced in that step, and the node state.

comparisons.description: The single commit step empties the whole queued read set at once.
Every previously queued request is re-admitted into unconfirmedReads in that same step.
That one step emits one heartbeat per released request, so the retained queue also becomes a burst of outbound messages.

knowledge.assertion: releasePendingReadIndexMessages drains the queue through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, one response per queued message
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry

scope.description: Control for the growth claim: repeat the same-context ReadIndex retry pattern on a leader with CheckQuorum enabled, tick through an election timeout so the leader loses its quorum view, and record whether growth stops and whether the accumulated queue is reclaimed.
assumptions: Real raft instance built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum set true over voters {1,2,3}, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe; no peer messages are delivered, so the quorum view is empty.
Retries are submitted in batches of eight between ticks (24 in total before the leader steps down), all with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract assigns to callers.
After the step-down eight more retries are submitted, so the harness also observes what a follower with no leader does with a read request.
excluded: Any claim that CheckQuorum is required or recommended for ReadOnlySafe; it is only used here as the competing liveness mechanism.
Any measurement of a network partition; the quorum view is emptied by delivering no messages.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexGrowthWithCheckQuorum builds newTestConfig(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), sets CheckQuorum true, constructs the raft with newRaft, promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and clears the outbound buffers. It emits a setup event (check_quorum, state, election timeout, voter count), then loops up to three ticks submitting eight same-context MsgReadIndex messages per tick while clearing outbound traffic, and emits a before event with the accumulated queue length, state and whether the window closed. It then submits eight more retries after the step-down and emits an after event with the queue length before and after, a boolean showing they are equal, the node state and the unconfirmed length.

comparisons.description: With CheckQuorum enabled the leader loses its quorum view within the election timeout, so the growth window does close on its own under that configuration.
Closing the window does not reclaim what was accumulated: further read requests after the step-down leave the queue at its previous length.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by an authority transition

scope.description: Measure how much caller-supplied payload the leader retains when many distinct ReadIndex requests are accepted while it cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, and verify that each retained payload is a distinct buffer rather than one shared slice counted repeatedly.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every read takes the queued path.

64 requests are submitted, each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit).

Retention is summed over the Data fields of the entries held in pendingReadIndexMessages, and the number of distinct backing buffers is counted by taking the address of each buffer's first byte, so a shared slice would appear as distinct_ctx_buffers < pending.
excluded: Any claim about total process footprint (allocator overhead, per-message structs and slice headers are not counted) or about a specific deployment's memory limit.
Any claim that a caller must not send large contexts; only that the library accepts and retains whatever it is given.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexRetainedBytes builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, and emits a setup event with CheckQuorum, state, voter count, the per-request context size and the round count. It then submits 64 MsgReadIndex messages, each with its own 4096-byte Data buffer, clearing outbound traffic each round, and finally emits a probe event with the pending queue length, the summed retained Data length, the number of distinct backing buffers and the node state.

comparisons.description: Every one of the 64 distinct read requests is retained.
The retained caller payload is 64 times 4096 bytes, i.e. the retry count multiplied by the caller-chosen context size.
The byte total is genuine retention: the 64 payloads sit in 64 distinct buffers, so the sum is not one shared slice counted repeatedly.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path retains one message per request and is not reclaimed

scope.description: Drive a real raft through entering a joint configuration and then through proposing and applying an empty ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition, recording whether propose-time validation keeps the entry and whether applying it panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and the library defaults; the joint configuration is entered by applying ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and a single add-node change, which is the normal EnterJoint path.

The malformed change is submitted through raft.Step as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 built by marshalling ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit}, which is exactly the input shape an application or client would produce.

ApplyConfChange is invoked directly on the same instance because the entry would not be committed on a quorum-less test instance; no production logic is modified and the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data.
excluded: Any claim about how a client library or etcd constructs its ConfChangeV2 messages; only the library's own acceptance and apply paths are measured.
The Auto-transition empty change, which is the supported leave-joint idiom and is not part of this comparison.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, applies ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]} and emits a setup event with the resulting voters, outgoing voters, the tested transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then marshals ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, and emits an event with the step error, how many entries were appended and the type of the last entry. Finally it calls applyConfChange on that same change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: Propose-time validation kept the entry as a configuration change rather than replacing it, so the library accepted the request.
Applying the accepted change panics because Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passes validation and panics on apply

materials.text:
'MsgProp' proposes to append data to its log entries. This is a special
	type to redirect proposals to leader. Therefore, send method overwrites
	raftpb.Message's term with its HardState's term to avoid attaching its
	local term to 'MsgProp'. When 'MsgProp' is passed to the leader's 'Step'
	method, the leader first calls the 'appendEntry' method to append entries
	to its log, and then calls 'bcastAppend' method to send those entries to
	its peers. When passed to candidate, 'MsgProp' is dropped. When passed to
	follower, 'MsgProp' is stored in follower's mailbox(msgs) by the send
	method. It is stored with sender's ID and later forwarded to leader by
	rafthttp package.

func newRaft(c *Config) *raft {
	if err := c.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(err.Error())
	}
	raftlog := newLogWithSize(c.Storage, c.Logger, entryEncodingSize(c.MaxCommittedSizePerReady))
	hs, cs, err := c.Storage.InitialState()
	if err != nil {
		panic(err) // TODO(bdarnell)
	}

	r := &raft{
		id:                          c.ID,
		lead:                        None,
		isLearner:                   false,
		raftLog:                     raftlog,
		maxMsgSize:                  entryEncodingSize(c.MaxSizePerMsg),
		maxUncommittedSize:          entryPayloadSize(c.MaxUncommittedEntriesSize),
		trk:                         tracker.MakeProgressTracker(c.MaxInflightMsgs, c.MaxInflightBytes),
		electionTimeout:             c.ElectionTick,
		heartbeatTimeout:            c.HeartbeatTick,
		logger:                      c.Logger,
		checkQuorum:                 c.CheckQuorum,
		preVote:                     c.PreVote,
		readOnly:                    newReadOnly(c.ReadOnlyOption),
		disableProposalForwarding:   c.DisableProposalForwarding,
		disableConfChangeValidation: c.DisableConfChangeValidation,
		stepDownOnRemoval:           c.StepDownOnRemoval,
		traceLogger:                 c.TraceLogger,
	}

	traceInitState(r)
